non_blocking_issues: Coverage gap (safe direction, INFERRED from RevenueCat docs + code): RC's per-subscription `original_purchase_date` is the date the subscription GROUP first started and 'does not update for product changes within a subscription group or re-subscriptions by lapsed subscribers' (sdk.revenuecat.com SubscriptionInfo.originalPurchaseDate; api-v1 example shows `annual` and `onemonth` rows sharing one original_purchase_date). A pending purchase journaled for a product bought via crossgrade (e.g. monthly->annual) and later renewed therefore has evidence.purchasedAt != original_purchase_date and stays `pending` forever under subscriptionLineageRow() (index.ts:3129). No false verdict is produced; the objective is met for the first-product lineage only.

Design divergence (non-monetary): for a DIRECT match, refunded_at + active entitlement returns `pending` (HOLD, index.ts:3180-3188); for a LINEAGE row the refund branch is skipped and the same contradictory state returns `fulfilled` (index.ts:3191; pinned by the new test 'a refund recorded on the lineage is not attributed to the original transaction'). The test's inline comment says 'nothing terminal is claimed' but asserts `fulfilled`, which the device treats as terminal (accessStore.ts:544-560 removes the journal entry). Consequence is only journal closure while RC already reports premium; entitlement truth is unaffected.

Pre-existing precision assumption (not introduced here): both the direct match and the new lineage match compare RC's second-precision ISO dates to the device's `purchasedAt` (StoreTransaction.purchaseDate -> toISOString) as exact strings after isoTimestamp() normalisation; a millisecond component on the device side would defeat both.

implement.summary: Defect on BASE_SHA (supabase/functions/api/index.ts, billingFulfilmentOf, lines ~3159-3170 on base): direct fulfilment evidence is matched only by `providerTransactionIdentity(row) === transactionId && isoTimestamp(row.purchase_date) === purchasedAt` against `subscriptions[productId]` and `non_subscriptions[productId]`. RevenueCat's subscriptions[product] row carries only the LATEST transaction (store_transaction_id/purchase_date), so once a renewal replaces the journaled purchase the journaled id is present nowhere and `matching.length !== 1` returns `pending` forever (base run: 12/26 new tests fail with outcome 'pending' where 'fulfilled'/'expired' is expected). Prior r1 (d0552ac2) anchored lineage proof to `original_purchase_date === purchasedAt`, so a resubscription after a lapse or an upgrade inside the group stayed pending (adversary breaks #1, #2), and it had no upper bound on the latest purchase date (break #3). Fix (commit 712366f2, only index.ts): new `subscriptionLineageRow(subscription, transactionId, purchasedAt, checkedAt)` — used ONLY when the journaled id is identified by no candidate row for the product (an id present at another date remains a conflict → pending; lifetime/non_subscription rows never form a lineage) — proves the lineage when `original_purchase_date <= purchasedAt < purchase_date`, the latest transaction has a valid store_transaction_id different from the journaled id, and `purchase_date <= checkedAt` (verifiedAt). The verdict then follows the lineage's access state: active entitlement for the product → fulfilled; otherwise the existing explicit-expiry+grace rule → expired, malformed → pending. A refunded_at on a renewal-headed lineage is never attributed to the journaled transaction (verdict follows access state instead). The direct-match path is unchanged. Adversary file attack_w07_02_renewal_lineage.test.ts (not committed) run against HEAD: 14/15 pass; the one failing assertion (ATTACK 11 sub-second case: evidence 500 ms after original_purchase_date must stay pending) encodes r1's equality anchoring and is inherently incompatible with fixing breaks #1/#2 — under the lineage-window rule it fulfils.
